title: Large-scale GPU data pipelines
subtitle: A generation pipeline that populated tens of millions of dataset items on two consumer GPUs, with persistent item identities, lease-based claiming and prompts baked at build time for cache reuse.

stats.label: probes submitted in one captured window
probes per second, with zero retries
hidden-state extractions over 10.8 M tokens, 7B dense model in FP8

lede: FAFO Core and Function Forge: my distillation research needed tens of millions of model-generated dataset items. Each one had to trace back to the knowledge it came from, and they had to be produced fast enough to keep two consumer GPUs saturated. I treated that as an industrial data pipeline, and I let the workload itself decide what the substrate needed. The probe generator is a Rust function on the FAFO Core substrate. It reads a unified work view over three source types, assembles class-specific prompts, submits them to the GPU broker, and stores each result as a token-ID array with provenance. It runs in service mode with queue-depth triggers.
quote: A research result that cannot be reproduced is worth little.
evidence: High-throughput batch inference: tens of millions of traceable dataset items on two NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs, 876K probes and 131 M tokens in one window at 156/s with zero retries.
Prefix-cache engineering: prompts tokenized at build time and baked into the binary so every class shares a byte-identical prefix the inference engine reuses from cache.
Reproducible ML data capture: hidden-state mining runs content-addressed and safe to resubmit, about 203K extractions over 10.8 M tokens from a 7B dense model in FP8.
author: Corey James
